params.body:
Three competitor reports reached the Observatory as source PDFs and were not caught: Crowd DNA ("How We Work As Cultural Strategists"), The People ("Add to Cart: The playbook…") and Archrival's Almanac ("ALMANAC: The Funnel is F*cked"). A report's source row is named after the title on its cover, which rarely names the publisher, so neither the audit nor the checks saw them; their signals were citable until they were marked by hand on 23 October 2026, and two published posts cited The People's report.

- `competitorOfSource` (competitors.mjs): a source row is a competitor by its name, its author, the file name in its notes or its id, with hyphens and underscores read as spaces ("Crowd-DNA-How-We-Work…"), or by its site. An author who is exactly a company's name counts even when that name alone is an ordinary phrase ("The People").
- `ingest-report.mjs` checks it when a report lands (upload, Drive or command line all pass here) and marks the source as read for inspiration only, saying why ("competitor list (Crowd DNA, by its file)"). The team still reads it in the Observatory; nothing of it is cited.
- `bin/competitor-audit.mjs` uses the same check for the rows already there, and says by what it found each one.

Tests: `competitors.test.mjs` with the three real cases and two that must not match (a NielsenIQ report, "The people of Europe" by Eurostat). Full suite 1350 of 1356, the 6 `report-render` failures need pdftoppm and fail on main too. `tsc` clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
params.title: A report by a competitor is caught by its author, file name or id, and marked when it lands
